cost: B annotation bytes, M mentions, N words: reading O(B+M²) worst case for rightmost-search/remove; writing filters all mentions per sentence and per word, conservative O(B+NM log M), O(B+M) temporary/output storage; span_head O(span width).
description: CorefUD bracket events, sentence-bounded mention stacks, normalized MISC output and tree-derived span heads.
forward: Scan values left to right. '(' emits Open(eid, first-hyphen remainder), ')' immediately emits Close for singletons; other text through ')' emits Close. Open appends (sent,start,MAX); Close removes the rightmost equal eid and sets inclusive end, rejecting no-open before cross-sentence. Final nonempty stack errors. Writer opens descending end then eid, closes descending start then eid; head field=head-start+1. span_head chooses external-parent candidates, minimum depth, nonpunctuation, lowest index; no candidates returns start.
inverse: R(y)={documents whose event fold produces ordered spans/eids/etype y}. Additional non-Entity MISC and discarded fields after etype are free. After rebuilding Document Entity views from written raw rows, valid sentence-bounded spans with stack-compatible same-eid nesting and writer-generated ids recover span/eid pairs (with the serialized e prefix), not original annotations or note/head text. Merely in-range spans are insufficient: crossing same-eid spans [0,2] and [1,3] read back as [0,3] and [1,2]. Existing Document Entity views remain stale after write. Head choice has multiple compatible trees.
limitations: No arbitrary malformed public rows/spans, allocation failure or full grammar proof. Writer zip truncation and unrefreshed derived views are modeled limitations.
Partial lexical syntax; no executable percentage surrogate; no corpus or universal proof.
state: Document sentences with optional Entity strings; read stack (eid, output index); writer mutates raw UdDoc rows/comments.
